hunt.name: Defender Weakening: Tamper Protection, ASR Rules and Exclusions
hunt.description:
Ransomware operators turn Defender down before they deploy. The usual moves are an exclusion for the staging folder, ASR rules switched to audit, Tamper Protection off, or the service stopped. Each one is ordinary admin work when it arrives through Group Policy or Intune, which is why a single rule rarely catches it.

Defender's own database, mpenginedb.db, keeps the engine's view of Tamper Protection and the ASR rule state changes it applied, and it stops filling when the engine stops recording. The defender_mpengine osquery extension decrypts it on each host. This hunt reads that state, adds the live exclusion list from the registry and the registry writes and commands that made the change, and stacks every change across the fleet. A change on one host stands apart from a policy rollout.

Hosts that were weakened by hand are then checked for what usually follows: payloads running from the excluded folders, shadow-copy and backup deletion, and Defender's own ransomware detections and rollback tracking.

meta.name: Defender Weakening: Tamper Protection, ASR Rules and Exclusions
meta.hypothesis: An operator with administrative rights on a Windows host has weakened Microsoft Defender before running tooling or ransomware: Tamper Protection off, ASR rules moved to audit or off, scan exclusions added, or the engine stopped, on one host rather than through fleet policy.
meta.rationale: Run across every Windows host; the comparison across the fleet is what separates policy from hands-on change. Look first at servers and at hosts with local exclusions. Paste the hosts weakening-triage names into scope_hosts before the follow-up steps.
meta.analysis: Every weakening action is also a routine admin action. The hunt decides by comparing each host with the rest of the fleet, by who made the change and with what, and by what ran afterwards, which no single rule on a registry write can do.

hunt.justification: An antivirus switched down on one host is the step before encryption in most ransomware intrusions, and it is the step that removes the alerts that would have caught what follows.

scenario.summary: An operator with administrative rights weakens Microsoft Defender on a host: Tamper Protection off, ASR rules downgraded, exclusions added or the engine stopped. The payload then runs from the excluded location and recovery is inhibited before encryption.

stages.name: ASR rules moved to audit or off
observables: Writes under Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR

stages.name: Payload from excluded folder and recovery inhibited

coverage.reason: How the operator obtained administrative rights is outside this hunt; it starts at the first change to Defender.

blind_spots.requires: the defender_mpengine osquery extension loaded by osqueryd (running as SYSTEM) on every Windows host, with Microsoft Defender Antivirus as the active engine and defender_mpengine_status.error empty
blind_spots.question: Did Defender record anything on hosts where the extension is missing, cannot decrypt the database, or Defender is passive behind another antivirus?
blind_spots.risk: Those hosts return no rows, which looks the same as a clean host. An attacker who has removed or stopped Defender also leaves an empty or stale database.
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy the extension through extensions.load on all Windows hosts and alert on defender_mpengine_status rows with a non-empty error.

blind_spots.requires: Microsoft documentation of the MpTamperProtectionState and ASR state values stored in AttributePersistContext
blind_spots.question: Does a recorded state mean off, audit or block?
blind_spots.risk: Values are read as stored. Protokol-7 notes the Tamper Protection record cannot be tied to attacker activity on its own: an administrator produces the same value.
blind_spots.remediation: Read the values on hosts whose configuration is known and record the mapping with this hunt.

blind_spots.requires: registry change telemetry (Sysmon event 13 or object-access auditing on the Defender keys) in hb_registry_activity
blind_spots.question: When was an exclusion added, and by which process?
blind_spots.risk: The registry table's mtime is per key, not per value, so one new exclusion dates the whole list. Without change telemetry the exclusion is visible but not attributable.

blind_spots.question: Is a stale database a stopped engine or a host where another antivirus is primary?
blind_spots.risk: With a third-party antivirus, Defender is passive or off and its database stops filling legitimately; antivirus_products in defender-engine-state shows which.

lookback_days.description: Days of history to examine. Defender keeps roughly two weeks in mpenginedb.db.

scope_hosts.description: Hosts to focus the follow-up queries on, as osquery reports their hostname; empty runs them across the estate.

config.description: Establish which hosts can answer and what state their engine is in. The extension's own status says whether the database decrypted; the newest attack-scoring and path-tag records say whether the engine is still writing; Windows Security Center says whether Defender is the active, up-to-date antivirus. A busy host whose newest record is days old has an engine that stopped recording.
config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, s.protection, s.key_source, s.quick_check, s.error, s.db_size, s.wal_size, (SELECT MAX(insert_time) FROM defender_mpengine_rolling_queues) AS newest_scoring_record, (SELECT MAX(insert_time) FROM defender_mpengine_persist_context) AS newest_path_record, (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(name || ' state=' || state || ' sigs=' || signatures_up_to_date, '; ') FROM windows_security_products WHERE type = 'Antivirus') AS antivirus_products, CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) AS checked_at FROM defender_mpengine_status s
config.expected_signal: One row per Windows host. error = '' and quick_check = 'ok' mean the host can answer. A non-empty error, a missing Defender entry or a Defender state other than On, or newest records far older than checked_at on an active host are findings in themselves. A host that returns no row has no extension.

primitive_config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, s.protection, s.key_source, s.quick_check, s.error, s.db_size, s.wal_size, (SELECT MAX(insert_time) FROM defender_mpengine_rolling_queues) AS newest_scoring_record, (SELECT MAX(insert_time) FROM defender_mpengine_persist_context) AS newest_path_record, (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(name || ' state=' || state || ' sigs=' || signatures_up_to_date, '; ') FROM windows_security_products WHERE type = 'Antivirus') AS antivirus_products, CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) AS checked_at FROM defender_mpengine_status s
primitive_config.label: Defender engine state per host
primitive_config.expected: One row per Windows host. error = '' and quick_check = 'ok' mean the host can answer. A non-empty error, a missing Defender entry or a Defender state other than On, or newest records far older than checked_at on an active host are findings in themselves. A host that returns no row has no extension.

nodes.label: Tamper Protection state recorded by the engine

config.description: Read the Tamper Protection state the engine persists. Protokol-7 recovered a record of it set to off from the WAL of a test machine; it is the one place the engine's own view of Tamper Protection is kept outside the registry.
config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, file_path, context AS recorded_state, insert_time, expire_time FROM defender_mpengine_persist_context WHERE file_path = 'MpTamperProtectionState' OR context LIKE '%TamperProtection%'
config.expected_signal: One row per host with the recorded state. A state meaning off on a host whose policy says on is the lead; the value is stored as Defender wrote it and is not documented, so compare it with hosts known to be correct.

primitive_config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, file_path, context AS recorded_state, insert_time, expire_time FROM defender_mpengine_persist_context WHERE file_path = 'MpTamperProtectionState' OR context LIKE '%TamperProtection%'
primitive_config.label: Tamper Protection state recorded by the engine
primitive_config.expected: One row per host with the recorded state. A state meaning off on a host whose policy says on is the lead; the value is stored as Defender wrote it and is not documented, so compare it with hosts known to be correct.

config.description: List the attack surface reduction rule state changes the engine recorded. A policy rollout changes the same rule to the same state on hundreds of hosts; an operator switching one rule to audit or off does it on one.
config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, asr_rule_id, asr_rule_name, context AS recorded_state, COUNT(*) AS records, MIN(insert_time) AS first_recorded, MAX(insert_time) AS last_recorded FROM defender_mpengine_persist_context WHERE record_kind = 'asr_rule_state' GROUP BY asr_rule_id, asr_rule_name, context
config.expected_signal: Rule and state pairs shared by most of the fleet are policy. A pair seen on fewer than three hosts, especially for the LSASS, Office child-process, PsExec/WMI or ransomware rules, is a lead.

primitive_config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, asr_rule_id, asr_rule_name, context AS recorded_state, COUNT(*) AS records, MIN(insert_time) AS first_recorded, MAX(insert_time) AS last_recorded FROM defender_mpengine_persist_context WHERE record_kind = 'asr_rule_state' GROUP BY asr_rule_id, asr_rule_name, context
primitive_config.label: ASR rule state changes
primitive_config.expected: Rule and state pairs shared by most of the fleet are policy. A pair seen on fewer than three hosts, especially for the LSASS, Office child-process, PsExec/WMI or ransomware rules, is a lead.

config.description: Inventory every path, process, extension and address excluded from scanning, local and policy. Exclusions are not in mpenginedb.db, but the registry holds them and osquery runs as SYSTEM, which can read them. An excluded folder is a folder the engine records nothing about.
config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, key AS exclusion_key, name AS excluded_item, CASE WHEN LOWER(key) LIKE '%\policies\%' THEN 'policy' ELSE 'local' END AS exclusion_source, mtime AS key_last_written FROM registry WHERE (key LIKE 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions\%' OR key LIKE 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions\%') AND name NOT IN ('', '(Default)')
config.expected_signal: Exclusions shared across a fleet segment are configuration. A local exclusion on one or two hosts, or one covering a user-writable folder, a whole drive, a script host or an archive extension, is a lead.

primitive_config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, key AS exclusion_key, name AS excluded_item, CASE WHEN LOWER(key) LIKE '%\policies\%' THEN 'policy' ELSE 'local' END AS exclusion_source, mtime AS key_last_written FROM registry WHERE (key LIKE 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions\%' OR key LIKE 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions\%') AND name NOT IN ('', '(Default)')
primitive_config.label: Defender exclusions configured now
primitive_config.expected: Exclusions shared across a fleet segment are configuration. A local exclusion on one or two hosts, or one covering a user-writable folder, a whole drive, a script host or an archive extension, is a lead.

config.description: Find who wrote Defender's exclusion, real-time protection, feature and ASR keys, and with what. This gives the time and the writing process that the registry inventory cannot.
config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, reg_key_path, reg_value_name, reg_value_data, process_name, process_cmd_line, actor_user_name FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND (LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%\windows defender\exclusions\%' OR LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%\windows defender\real-time protection%' OR LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%\windows defender\features%' OR LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%\windows defender exploit guard\asr%' OR (LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%\windows defender%' AND LOWER(reg_value_name) IN ('disableantispyware', 'disableantivirus', 'disablerealtimemonitoring', 'disablebehaviormonitoring', 'disableioavprotection', 'tamperprotection'))) AND LOWER(COALESCE(process_name, '')) NOT LIKE '%\msmpeng.exe'
config.expected_signal: Writes by the Group Policy or MDM client across many hosts are policy. A write by powershell.exe, reg.exe or an unknown binary on one host is a lead.

primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, reg_key_path, reg_value_name, reg_value_data, process_name, process_cmd_line, actor_user_name FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND (LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%\windows defender\exclusions\%' OR LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%\windows defender\real-time protection%' OR LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%\windows defender\features%' OR LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%\windows defender exploit guard\asr%' OR (LOWER(reg_key_path) LIKE '%\windows defender%' AND LOWER(reg_value_name) IN ('disableantispyware', 'disableantivirus', 'disablerealtimemonitoring', 'disablebehaviormonitoring', 'disableioavprotection', 'tamperprotection'))) AND LOWER(COALESCE(process_name, '')) NOT LIKE '%\msmpeng.exe'
primitive_config.label: Writes to Defender policy keys
primitive_config.expected: Writes by the Group Policy or MDM client across many hosts are policy. A write by powershell.exe, reg.exe or an unknown binary on one host is a lead.

config.description: Catch the commands operators use: Set-MpPreference and Add-MpPreference exclusions or switches, WMI MSFT_MpPreference, MpCmdRun -RemoveDefinitions, stopping WinDefend, and reg.exe edits of Defender keys.
config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, user_name, parent_process_name, process_name, process_cmd_line, integrity_level FROM hb_process_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND (((LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%set-mppreference%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%add-mppreference%') AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-exclusion%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-disable%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%attacksurfacereductionrules_actions%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-mapsreporting%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-submitsamplesconsent%')) OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%msft_mppreference%' OR (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%mpcmdrun%' AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-removedefinitions%') OR ((LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\sc.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\net.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\net1.exe') AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%windefend%') OR ((LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\reg.exe') AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%windows defender%'))
config.expected_signal: Rare outside deployment tooling. An interactive or service account running one of these outside a change window is the strongest single signal in this hunt.

primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, user_name, parent_process_name, process_name, process_cmd_line, integrity_level FROM hb_process_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND (((LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%set-mppreference%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%add-mppreference%') AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-exclusion%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-disable%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%attacksurfacereductionrules_actions%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-mapsreporting%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-submitsamplesconsent%')) OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%msft_mppreference%' OR (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%mpcmdrun%' AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-removedefinitions%') OR ((LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\sc.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\net.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\net1.exe') AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%windefend%') OR ((LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\reg.exe') AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%windows defender%'))
primitive_config.label: Commands that weaken Defender
primitive_config.expected: Rare outside deployment tooling. An interactive or service account running one of these outside a change window is the strongest single signal in this hunt.

nodes.label: Was Defender weakened, and by whom

config.description: Separate policy from hands-on weakening and decide which hosts to follow up.
config.objective: For each host, decide whether Defender was weakened in the window and how: Tamper Protection recorded off, an ASR rule moved to audit or off, a new exclusion, the engine stopped recording, or definitions removed. Treat a change that appears on many hosts within a short time and was written by the Group Policy or MDM client as policy. Treat a change on one host, made by PowerShell, reg.exe, sc.exe or WMI under a user or service account, or an exclusion of a user-writable folder, as hands-on. Hosts with no defender-engine-state row are unknown, not clean.
config.success_criteria: A per-host list of hands-on weakening with the change, the time, the account and the process, citing rows; the hosts to paste into scope_hosts; and the hosts that could not answer.

nodes.label: Execution and recovery inhibition after the change

config.description: Look for what weakening is usually for: binaries started from user-writable or excluded-looking folders, and the shadow-copy, backup, boot-recovery and log-clearing commands that come right before encryption.
config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, user_name, parent_process_name, process_name, process_cmd_line FROM hb_process_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND ((LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%vssadmin%delete%shadows%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%shadowcopy%delete%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%wbadmin%delete%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%bcdedit%recoveryenabled%no%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%wevtutil%cl %' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%cipher%/w%') OR (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%'))
config.expected_signal: Recovery-inhibition commands on a weakened host are close to conclusive. User-space binaries need the exclusions from defender-exclusions-now to judge: a binary running from an excluded folder is the payload the exclusion was made for.

primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, user_name, parent_process_name, process_name, process_cmd_line FROM hb_process_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND ((LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%vssadmin%delete%shadows%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%shadowcopy%delete%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%wbadmin%delete%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%bcdedit%recoveryenabled%no%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%wevtutil%cl %' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%cipher%/w%') OR (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%'))
primitive_config.label: Execution and recovery inhibition after the change
primitive_config.expected: Recovery-inhibition commands on a weakened host are close to conclusive. User-space binaries need the exclusions from defender-exclusions-now to judge: a binary running from an excluded folder is the payload the exclusion was made for.

nodes.label: Defender's ransomware detections and rollback tracking

config.description: Read what the engine itself concluded about ransomware on these hosts: detections with their remediation timeline, and the files and processes it started tracking for rollback.
config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, 'detection' AS record, detection_guid AS item, detection_time AS event_time, remediation_complete_time AS remediated_at, impacted_cbp_namespaces FROM defender_mpengine_ransomware_detections WHERE detection_time >= (CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) - {{lookback_days}} * 86400) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) || ',') > 0) UNION ALL SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, 'rollback_tracking' AS record, file_path AS item, instance_time AS event_time, NULL AS remediated_at, impacted_cbp_namespaces FROM defender_mpengine_backup_process_info WHERE instance_time >= (CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) - {{lookback_days}} * 86400) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) || ',') > 0)
config.expected_signal: Any detection row is serious. Rollback tracking of a binary from a user-writable path on a weakened host means the engine suspected it even with protection reduced.

primitive_config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, 'detection' AS record, detection_guid AS item, detection_time AS event_time, remediation_complete_time AS remediated_at, impacted_cbp_namespaces FROM defender_mpengine_ransomware_detections WHERE detection_time >= (CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) - {{lookback_days}} * 86400) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) || ',') > 0) UNION ALL SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, 'rollback_tracking' AS record, file_path AS item, instance_time AS event_time, NULL AS remediated_at, impacted_cbp_namespaces FROM defender_mpengine_backup_process_info WHERE instance_time >= (CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) - {{lookback_days}} * 86400) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) || ',') > 0)
primitive_config.label: Defender's ransomware detections and rollback tracking
primitive_config.expected: Any detection row is serious. Rollback tracking of a binary from a user-writable path on a weakened host means the engine suspected it even with protection reduced.

config.description: Join the weakening to what followed it.
config.objective: For each host from weakening-triage, decide whether the weakening was followed by attacker activity: recovery-inhibition commands, binaries running from excluded or user-writable folders, or Defender ransomware detections and rollback tracking. Order each host's evidence in time from the weakening onwards.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious, suspicious or benign per host, with a timeline that cites rows from each step.

config.description: Act on hands-on weakening; send anything unclear to a person.
config.condition: host-verdict finds at least one host where Defender was weakened by a change that is not fleet policy
config.question: host-verdict finds at least one host where Defender was weakened by a change that is not fleet policy

config.description: Stop what the weakening enabled, then put protection back.
config.instructions: Copy C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scans off the host first; the steps below change the records this hunt read. Isolate the host. Remove the exclusions that are not in the approved baseline, set the changed ASR rules back to block, turn Tamper Protection on from the management console, and run a full scan with current definitions.

config.description: Confirm each finding against change records and widen the search.
config.instructions: Check every weakened host against the change and deployment records for the window. For hands-on changes, find the account's other logons and run defender-tamper-commands across the estate for that account. Decrypt the copied Scans folder with the extension's --decrypt mode or Protokol-7's mpenginedb_parser, which also recovers deleted rows such as an earlier Tamper Protection state.

config.description: Record results and keep the signal.
config.instructions: Record weakened hosts and outcomes. Add approved exclusions to a baseline list so the next run shows only new ones. Schedule the pack queries defender_mpengine_tamper_protection and defender_mpengine_asr_rule_state with removed: true so state changes are logged as they happen, and alert on defender-tamper-commands.
